title: Analysis code and aggregated outputs: division of couples' labor earnings and meal-affordability deprivation in Türkiye (ILCS 2023–2025)
description:
Analysis code and aggregated outputs of a study of how the division of labor earnings between spouses is related to meal-affordability deprivation of their households, using the cross-sectional microdata of the 2023–2025 Income and Living Conditions Survey (ILCS), the Turkish implementation of EU-SILC. The unit of analysis is the reference couple of each household. Couples are classified by earner structure (husband-only, dual-earner and wife-only earner couples) and, among dual-earner couples, by the wife's share of the couple's net labor earnings. The analytic sample is restricted to a rectangular common support of the estimated earner-structure probabilities. Food deprivation is modeled with a weighted (pseudo-posterior) Bayesian multilevel logistic model (brms with CmdStan) with intercepts for NUTS-2 regions and for linkage chains of households observed in more than one survey year. Probabilities are standardized to the covariates of the common-support sample, marginalizing over the chain intercepts by Gauss–Hermite quadrature, and summarized as prespecified comparisons against a region of practical equivalence of ±2 percentage points. Secondary analyses (husband's status, survey years), sensitivity analyses and post hoc analyses of a time channel within the household (work intensity of the spouses, other adults in the household) are included. The outcome is the inability to afford a meal with meat, chicken or fish, or a vegetarian equivalent, every second day (a single material deprivation item).

The archive includes the R and Python code, 21 supplementary tables, 9 figures with their aggregated data, audit files, the analysis plan and its addendum. The repository contains no microdata; the TurkStat microdata must be obtained through TurkStat's official procedures. A manuscript is under review.
